text:
jia: noticed a weird tail latency bump on the continuous batcher after the kernel-handoff change, reproducing on canary cluster

sam: ugh, saw that in dashboards too. Is it only p99 or wider?

jia: p95->p99 jump mostly, median stable. seen on long prompts + high decode-rate requests

maria: any recent KV cache policy changes? sounds like more cache churn could blow up decode throughput

jia: i rolled kernel mapping to prefer fused-attn kernel for seq_len>1024, plus small change to token_budget target calc (more aggressive batching). KV stats show increased eviction rate around the bump window

leo: can you paste the perf trace? low overhead sample will help.

jia: pasting flame snippet and admission summary:
```
# admission sample (canary node 12)
admit_pool: continuous
batch_size_median: 12
token_budget_target: 4096 -> 6144 (after change)
kv_evictions_per_min: 78 -> 240
decode_tokens/s: 1200 -> 950 (tail)
```

alex: kv_evictions x3 is huge. likely more KV misses causing re-prefetch and kernel hot-switch thrash. We should validate kernel chosen per-batch not per-request.

sam: good call. current code lets kernel selector run per-batch but batch composition varies. if a batch mixes short+long decodes and kernel flip happens mid-batch, perf can regress

maria: also token_budget bump means batches target bigger token budgets -> bigger batches -> more within-batch heterogeneity. that can amplify the kernel-selection oscillation

leo: quick experiment idea: limit token_budget growth for mixed-length cohorts. set token_budget_delta to 0 for decode_rate_bucket >= high and prompt_length variance > threshold

jia: can patch param in runtime config and smoke on canary. patch: 
```yaml
batching:
  token_budget: 6144
  token_budget_safety_delta: 0  # disable aggressive expansion for mixed batches
  kernel_stickiness_ms: 200     # prefer current kernel for short window
```

alex: kernel_stickiness looks promising. also add metric export: "kernel_switches_per_min" and "kv_misses_per_batch"

perfbot: perfbot detected config change on canary cluster 5 minutes ago (user:jia)

sam: running canary run now. will route 5% traffic through patched nodes and capture p50/p95/p99 and kv evictions

maria: if that stabilizes tail we'll need to tune classification: split prompt_length buckets at 256/1024 and decode_rate buckets at 10/50 tok/s, then force strict cohorting so batches don't mix decode-rate strata

jia: noted. i'm drafting a short experiment plan:
- apply stickiness + zero delta on canary
- add kernel_switch and kv_miss metrics
- create cohorting rule: strict_bucket_mixing: false for mixed decode_rate prompts
- run 4h canary, collect p50/p95/p99 + kv_evictions + kernel_switches

leo: timeline?

jia: applying now, will report back in 30m then 4h summary

sam: 30m quick look: p95 down ~12%, p99 down ~18% on canary. kv_evictions down to ~90/min. kernel_switches_per_min dropped 70%

maria: great. suggests the interplay of token_budget and kernel flips was the root cause

alex: next steps: revert token_budget target change from global to per-cohort based, and add an admission prefilter that rejects high-variance batches (or splits them)

jia: agree. i'll open PR for per-cohort targets + admission-split. tagging @eng-runtime for review

sam: thanks. if anyone sees similar on prod, alert and we'll escalate to rollback. :thumbsup:

perfbot: canary metrics snapshot uploaded to /s3/redwood/perf/canary/2785412345.zip

jia: closing loop once PR is merged and rollout verified. thanks all.
